page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server instance featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU. The instance is provisioned with 0.3333 of a physical A40 GPU, delivering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor configured with 8 shared vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 40.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 5.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, contrasted by top-tier capabilities in specific machine learning workloads. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68 and a multi-core score of 14175.12, while the PassMark CPU score registered at 14090.9. Memory bandwidth tests showed a read-only small block speed of 784.94 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 52.63 GB/sec. In contrast to these average general-compute metrics, the fractional GPU configuration achieved top-tier results in low-to-medium parameter large language model inference. For a 135M model, prompt processing reached 9944.32 tokens per second and text generation reached 464.42 tokens per second. For a 7B model, prompt processing achieved 3147.67 tokens per second with text generation at 107.73 tokens per second.

The fractional GPU allocation offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not demand a full, dedicated A40 accelerator. By sharing the physical GPU and utilizing shared Intel vCPUs, this instance lowers the entry barrier for GPU-based tasks. However, the shared CPU allocation and average general-purpose benchmark scores present a tradeoff for CPU-bound tasks. This server is suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, database operations, and applications requiring moderate GPU acceleration alongside local NVMe storage.
